sections.title: Revolve and Revolve Cut
sections.text: Profiles uses the common canvas selector: choose regions, connected contours or individual entities rather than automatically consuming a whole multi-profile sketch. A flat model face can be a profile too, as for Extrude; its axis must then be a reference axis, a model edge or face, or a line of a sketch (a face has no sketch axes). Coplanar selections can be combined. Whole-sketch selection remains available explicitly and older files remain compatible. Choose Select axis in canvas separately from the profiles. The axis may be a sketch axis, a line in an earlier sketch (including construction geometry), a reference axis, a straight/circular model edge or a cylindrical face. Project axis into profile plane projects its origin and direction onto the selected profile plane; a perpendicular axis cannot be projected. Return to Select profiles in canvas to edit the profile selection. Extent is Full (360°), Angle, Up To Vertex or Up To Surface. Up To Vertex turns the profile round the axis until it reaches the vertex (click a model vertex, or choose a reference point); Up To Surface until it reaches a plane or flat face. A plane through the axis stops the revolution at whichever half of it comes first; another plane or face trims the revolution where it crosses it, keeping what lies on the profile's side. Reverse direction turns the other way round. A vertex on the axis, a surface through the profile and a surface the revolution never reaches are refused (a profile touching the axis needs an end plane through the axis). Surface Revolve goes up to them too. Angle supports One side, Two sides with independent angles, or Symmetric (the total angle split equally). Reverse exchanges the signed direction for one/two sides. The total angle must not exceed 360°. Profiles must not cross a coplanar rotation axis. Full ignores stored angle values. Older files whose angles were clamped to 360° keep that geometry and migrate to Full when edited. Operation offers Join, New body, Cut or Intersect (as for Extrude; Sweep and Loft offer the same). Thin Feature revolves a wall along open or closed contours; open contours enable it automatically. Cuts have the same Feature Scope as Extrude; Select target bodies in canvas switches explicitly from profile/axis selection to target-body picking.

sections.title: Sweep and Sweep Cut
sections.text: Sweeps a profile along a path. Profile: a selected sketch region or contour, or Circular with a diameter (useful for springs). Path: a selected sketch chain, 3D sketch, curve or helix; or, under Path from Model Edges → Select model edges, edges of the model joined end to end into one chain (open or closed, without branches). A chain of model edges is followed from its end in the profile's plane. Orientation: Perpendicular to path keeps the section square to the path; Parallel to initial profile moves it along the path without turning it (tight bends can make the sweep invalid); Square to faces it runs on keeps the profile's plane through the normal of the faces chosen with Select faces in canvas, for a path that lies on them (a groove round a curved part). Twist angle (with Perpendicular): the profile turns by this total angle along the path, by distance: Twist → Evenly along the path, or Eased in and out (slowly at both ends, fastest half way). Positive angles turn by the right-hand rule along the path. Equations are allowed; 0 is the usual sweep. A twist needs an open path with no sharp corners (round them first), and the profile in the plane square to the path at its start. End scale (without a guide): the profile grows or shrinks about the path from its own size at the start to End scale times it at the end, by the length along the path, evenly or (Scale → Eased in and out) slowly at both ends; 1 keeps its size. It works with every orientation and with a twist. Checked against the volumes integrated along a line and an arc to 1e-7. Guide (optional): a second curve (sketch chain, 3D sketch, curve or helix) the profile follows. It replaces Orientation and Twist; removing it brings them back. Guide controls → Orientation: the profile turns to keep facing the guide and keeps its size. The guide doesn't have to touch the profile. Guide controls → Section size: the profile is scaled evenly so its edge stays on the guide. The guide starts on the profile's edge and crosses each plane square to the path once. A guided sweep takes one closed profile without holes or Thin, an open path and an open guide. Both curves run between the planes square to the path at its ends, and don't touch. A guide drawn the other way round is turned automatically. Contact with the guide is checked to 0.0001 mm; geometry that doesn't fit gives an error rather than an ordinary sweep. Thin option (without a guide). Select Profile / Path / Guide in canvas activates one role at a time. Click inside a closed profile or on its contour; click path and guide curves directly. Each role has its own Chain selection checkbox. Turn it off to pick individual connected entities from one sketch, then choose Use selected contour or press Enter. Add or clear an unfinished contour before switching roles. Paths and guides may include construction curves. Different contours from the same sketch can be used in different roles, but the same entities cannot be reused across roles. Unrelated sketch geometry is ignored by selected contour references; missing selected curves report an error. Other sources (whole sketch / curve) retains explicit whole-sketch and supported derived-curve selection, including existing files. Solid Sweep uses the same Join / New body / Cut operation control as Extrude and Revolve. Cut supports explicit target-body selection. Without a guide, selected regions retain internal holes and open profiles can use Thin Feature.

  • Path: a selected sketch chain, 3D sketch, curve or helix; or, under Path from Model Edges → Select model edges, edges of the model joined end to end into one chain (open or closed, without branches). A chain of model edges is followed from its end in the profile's plane.
  • Orientation: Perpendicular to path keeps the section square to the path; Parallel to initial profile moves it along the path without turning it (tight bends can make the sweep invalid); Square to faces it runs on keeps the profile's plane through the normal of the faces chosen with Select faces in canvas, for a path that lies on them (a groove round a curved part).
  • Twist angle (with Perpendicular): the profile turns by this total angle along the path, by distance: Twist → Evenly along the path, or Eased in and out (slowly at both ends, fastest half way). Positive angles turn by the right-hand rule along the path. Equations are allowed; 0 is the usual sweep. A twist needs an open path with no sharp corners (round them first), and the profile in the plane square to the path at its start.
  • End scale (without a guide): the profile grows or shrinks about the path from its own size at the start to End scale times it at the end, by the length along the path, evenly or (Scale → Eased in and out) slowly at both ends; 1 keeps its size. A guide drawn the other way round is turned automatically. Contact with the guide is checked to 0.0001 mm; geometry that doesn't fit gives an error rather than an ordinary sweep.
  • Thin option (without a guide).

sections.title: Loft and Loft Cut
sections.text: Blends between two or more section profiles, in order. A third or later profile shapes the middle. Activate Select profiles in canvas, then click a sketch contour or inside a closed region. Multiple regions in one sketch can be selected independently; holes belong to their enclosing region. Select guides in canvas switches to guide selection, including construction curves. Source sketches are temporarily shown while selecting, without changing their saved visibility. Chain selection picks connected curves automatically. Turn it off to select individual segments from one sketch, then choose Add selected contour or press Enter. Escape clears an unfinished selection. Profiles and guides have separate ordered lists with move and remove controls, matching numbered highlights in the canvas. Other sources retains whole-sketch and supported 3D curve selection. Stored contour references follow source curve IDs through edits and renaming; missing or ambiguous boundaries report an error. Surface Loft uses the same contour selection for open or closed sections. Guide contacts are checked against the actual CAD profiles. The fit uses the original guide curves and refines intermediate sections until sampled distances to the CAD faces are within 0.01 mm. If this check fails, the feature reports an error: add a section near a tight bend. These are sampled numerical checks, not a guarantee over every point of the continuous curve. Thin lofts retain the wall's offset from the sketched guide. Guide construction → CAD constraints (two profiles) builds patches constrained directly by the original 3D guide edges. It checks the kernel's contact error and independent distances against 0.0001 mm. This method currently requires two profiles without Thin Feature, with guides starting and ending on corresponding patches. Holes in the profiles are lofted between them without the guides (each hole's sections joined directly) and cut out of the guided outline; they must stay inside it. Across guide seams selects C0 (contact, the default), G1 (tangent joins) or G2 (curvature-continuous joins along shared guides). Original profile corners are preserved. Unsupported or incompatible constraints report an error without falling back to approximation. Adaptive approximation remains available for the broader set of loft options and is the default for existing features.

sections.title: Profile correspondence
sections.text: Enable Edit profile connectors to display numbered connections between matching profile vertices. Use Pick start in canvas, choose a start vertex in the panel, or drag a connector endpoint to another existing vertex on that profile. Moving an attachment shifts the correspondence around the contour while preserving boundary order. For circles, set the seam angle (expressions are supported) or drag the seam in the canvas. Open surface profiles use their endpoints; reversing their direction exchanges the endpoints. Settings follow the selected profile through renaming, reordering, save/reopen and source edits. A deleted attachment reports an error and must be reselected. Use a profile's Automatic for this profile button to clear its settings, or reset all connectors to return to automatic matching. Closed profiles must share the same traversal direction: reversing only some would fold the loft. Manual matching is passed to the CAD builder without automatic remapping and also applies when guides or endpoint conditions are used. Manual connectors support sketch profiles. Start vertex → Inside a curve… (or dragging a connector onto a curve between vertices) starts the profile at a point inside one of its curves, Along it a share of the curve's length in its own direction (expressions allowed): the profile gains a point there, without splitting the sketch, so a triangle can be lofted to a square by starting the triangle inside one of its edges. Every profile must end up with the same number of points. Profiles with holes list each hole: Hole 1, Hole 2… choose which of this profile's holes goes with the other profiles' hole of that number (pair them by hand when the automatic pairing joins the wrong ones), and Hole … start sets where each hole starts (a vertex, inside a curve, or a seam angle for a circle), as for the outline. Thin lofts take the connectors too: each wall starts at its vertex nearest the profile's start. 3D curve profiles use automatic matching. More connectors: after a profile's start vertex, Add connector adds another vertex to pair (Connector 2, 3…), so profiles with different numbers of corners can be matched corner to corner as you choose (a square's four corners to four of a hexagon's six). Every profile needs the same number of connectors, in the same order round it; between two connectors, the profile with fewer sides has its longest ones halved until the sides pair one to one. Connectors in a different order round one profile would make the loft's sides cross, and are refused. Surface Loft uses the same controls.

sections.title: Start and end conditions
sections.text: Start Condition and End Condition control the first and last section independently: Free preserves the usual loft when both ends are free. Normal to profile makes the longitudinal endpoint derivative normal to its planar sketch. Direction uses a world axis or a reference axis. Create a reference axis from a sketch line for an inclined direction. Tangent to adjacent faces (G1) matches the tangent planes of existing solid or surface faces along the endpoint profile. Click Select start support faces or Select end support faces, then click the adjacent side faces in the canvas. Select all faces needed to cover the outer and inner profile edges, including Thin walls: one cylindrical face can cover a circle; a rectangular extrusion needs its four side faces. For a hollow section also select the adjacent inner walls. The profile must coincide with their boundary, not merely lie inside a face. Click Select profiles in canvas to return to contour selection. Curvature to adjacent faces (G2) also matches the curvature of the selected adjacent faces. Set this independently at either end, including G2 at both ends or a G1/G2 combination. It uses the same support-face selection rules as G1. Curvature is measured on the CAD surfaces, including the along-edge, across-edge and mixed components; incompatible geometry reports an error. A sampled CAD normal check also rejects detected local collapses between profiles; reduce Influence or add a section if this happens. This does not certify the absence of every possible self-intersection. Influence is a positive multiplier of the endpoint derivative length; 1 uses the distance to the neighboring profile as the scale. Larger values extend the endpoint's influence farther into the loft. Expressions are supported. Reverse tangent direction reverses the signed derivative and may create an invalid or overlapping loft. Endpoint conditions require matching profile curve counts and a smooth loft. Solid lofts support internal holes and Thin Feature, including Outside, Inside and Mid-plane sketch offsets and open Thin profiles. Every section must have the same number of corresponding inner loops. Outer and inner walls are constructed together and sewn to end faces with openings, rather than filling the cavities. G1 and G2 support selection must cover all walls. They support two or more sections, and closed profiles for solids or open/closed profiles for surfaces. Intermediate sections use C2 cubic interpolation. Normal to profile requires a planar sketch; Direction also supports curve sources in Surface Loft. Closed surface profiles stay uncapped. Guide curves with endpoint conditions use Adaptive approximation. Guides must meet every section in order, and their endpoint tangents must agree with the requested tangent planes and direction. Conflicting constraints report an error. Refinement uses 8/16/32/64/128 intermediate stations per profile interval and checks independent native guide points against the final CAD side faces to 0.0001 mm. With Thin, guide checks retain the sketched outline’s offset to the outer wall; inner loops follow the guide deformation. Multiple guide deformations blend smoothly between contact locations (C2 blend weights), preserving physical profile corners. Influence remains relative to the original neighboring section, independently of the refinement count. CAD constraints with C0/G1/G2 guide seams still requires free endpoint conditions; selecting it with endpoint constraints gives an explicit error instead of switching methods. The kernel constructs clamped tensor B-splines (cubic, or degree five along the loft when G2 is requested), refining profile interpolation from 8 through 128 intervals. It checks off-node profile contact and endpoint derivatives, including influence and direction. Final sewn CAD faces are checked again at 33 positions per endpoint for contact within 0.0001 mm, tangent-plane mismatch within 0.5°, and relative endpoint derivative error within 0.0001. These are sampled numerical checks, not a certified global bound. Unsupported or incompatible constraints report an error without dropping the endpoint conditions. G2 additionally compares all three components of the second fundamental form on the final CAD faces, with curvature mismatch at most 0.001 1/mm. Feature notes report measured contact, angular and G2 curvature errors. A circle is split into as many equal arcs as the other profile has corners. Profiles with different segment counts give an error naming the sketches. Options: straight (ruled) sides, Thin. Without straight sides: Through the profiles curvature-continuous (C2) or tangent-continuous (C1), and Smooth the surface, which evens out its bends. Guide Curves (optional): curves the loft's outline follows between the profiles, such as a body's outline seen from the side. Each runs from the first profile to the last, through every profile, and is a selected chain of sketch curves or a supported curve source. Separate guides can come from the same sketch. One guide pulls the loft along it; two or more shape it round the outline, each where it touches the profiles. The profiles themselves are kept as drawn. Holes in the profiles, and a thin loft's inside, move with the outline, so a thin wall keeps its thickness; for a thin loft, draw the guide on the sketched line.

sections.title: Hole
sections.text: Hole (Features tab, Insert ▸ Features ▸ Hole…) makes standard holes. Type Sizes --- --- Hole (clearance) ISO 273 close, normal or loose fit, for M2 to M24 Counterbore For socket head cap screws (ISO 4762) Countersink ISO 10642, 90° Tapped hole ISO metric or Unified (inch), drilled at the tap drill size; the thread is shown as a cosmetic thread and given in drawing callouts Counterdrill A wider drill (standard sizes: the counterbore's diameter and depth) with a drill point of its own angle down to the hole Slot Two half circles of the hole's diameter joined: Slot length between their centres, Slot angle from the face's X direction Custom sizes Your own diameters and depths End: Blind (with a Drill point of Drill point angle, 118° unless set), Through All, Up To Next (each hole until its axis first comes out of the material: through the wall it starts in), Up To Vertex, Up To Surface and Offset From Surface (a plane or flat face, picked in the canvas or chosen in the list; each hole's own depth along its axis); reversible. Far-side countersink (Through All, Up To Next): a countersink of its own diameter and angle where the hole comes out (the far side of the first wall for Up To Next, of the last for Through All). Place holes at clicked points on a face, or exactly at the points and circle centres of a sketch on the face. On a curved face (a shaft, a pipe) a hole is drilled square to the face where it was clicked: a radial hole. Holes work on sheet metal too, and a drawing's Hole Callout reads their size from the feature.

sections.title: Helix
sections.text: Pick a sketch with a circle; it sets the axis and diameter. Define the helix by pitch and revolutions, pitch and height, or height and revolutions. Options: start angle, clockwise, reverse. Use a helix as a sweep path for springs and coils.

sections.title: Thread Cut and Thread Extrude
sections.text: Click a bore (Thread Cut) or a shaft (Thread Extrude). The size is chosen automatically from the diameter, or choose a metric (ISO) or inch (Unified) standard size, or custom. Coarse / UNC sizes are preferred. Optional pitch; left-hand option. Length: the whole face, a depth, or up to a plane or face. Threads never reach past the ends of their face. The bore or shaft is resized to the thread size if needed (a bore to the minor diameter, a shaft to the major). A bore that would break out of the body is refused. Threads run all the way to the ends: grooves run out into open air, otherwise the thread is cut off flush with the end.

  • Length: the whole face, a depth, or up to a plane or face. Threads never reach past the ends of their face.

sections.title: Cosmetic Thread
sections.text: Cosmetic Thread (Features tab, Insert ▸ Features ▸ Cosmetic Thread…) marks a bore or shaft as threaded without modelling the thread, so it costs nothing to rebuild. Use it where the thread only needs to be shown and called out. Click the bore (internal thread) or the shaft (external thread). The thread starts at the end nearest the click; Start from the other end reverses it. Size, pitch, left-hand and length (whole face, depth, or up to a plane or face) as for Thread Cut. The feature's note says when the face is not the size the thread expects (a bore about the minor diameter, a shaft the major). In the model it shows as a thin helix on the face. Tapped holes made with the Hole feature show their threads the same way. On drawings it is drawn by convention: from the side, thin lines at the thread's other diameter and a line where it ends, dashed for a hidden bore; end on, a three-quarter circle. A view's Cosmetic threads box turns them off. Hole Callout on a bore with a cosmetic thread gives the thread, for example "M10×1.5 THRU ALL / TAP DRILL Ø8.5 THRU ALL".

sections.title: Wrap (Emboss / Deboss)
sections.text: Pick a sketch (outlines and/or text) and a face, flat or curved. The sketch is projected along its normal onto the face and raised (emboss) or sunk (deboss) by the depth.

sections.title: Patterns and Mirror
sections.text: Patterns and mirrors copy features or bodies. Any feature that changes the bodies at a place can be copied: extrudes, cuts, holes, fillets, chamfers, drafts, domes and sheet metal forms. A feature without a shape of its own (such as a fillet) is run again on the matching edges or faces of each copy. Feature Copies --- --- Linear Pattern Along one or two directions (X, Y, Z or any reference axis) Circular Pattern Round an axis (X, Y, Z or any reference axis) Mirror About a plane or flat face Sketch Driven Pattern At every point (or circle centre) of a sketch Curve Driven Pattern Along a sketch, 3D sketch or helix, spaced evenly to the end or at a set distance; moved, or turned to follow the curve Table Driven Pattern A copy for each row of a table: x, y from the feature along a plane's directions (the feature's own sketch plane when none is chosen) and optionally an angle turning the copy about the plane's normal through the feature. Rows are separated by ; or new lines, cells by commas, tabs or spaces, so a table pasted from a spreadsheet works (a header row is skipped); cells can be sums or use variables Fill Pattern On a square or staggered grid over a flat face, kept a margin from its edges (for example a perforated panel) Linear Pattern options : Distance → From the first to the last spreads the instances over a total length instead of setting the spacing between each two. Spacing grows by makes each spacing that much more than the one before (a negative value: less), for copies that spread out or close up. Symmetric adds as many again the other way from the feature. With a second direction, Pattern the feature only copies just the feature along it, not the whole first row (an L of copies). Circular Pattern options : Angle grows by (without equal spacing) makes each angle between copies that much more than the one before. Symmetric adds as many again the other way round (less than a whole turn). Rings makes rings of copies further out from the axis, Ring spacing apart, out through the feature's middle. Instances to Skip (Linear and Circular) : instance numbers to leave out, separated by commas: 1 is the feature, 2 the first copy, -2 the first copy the other way (symmetric). With a second direction or rings, row.column: 3.2 is the third along the first direction (or round) in the second row (or ring). What to copy. Choose the Feature, and add any number of More features: each is copied the same way. In a Linear, Circular, Sketch Driven or Curve Driven Pattern, Clicking the model picks either Faces, where each face brings the feature that made it (click a hole's wall to copy the hole), or Bodies, which are copied whole to every place as new bodies. Mirror takes bodies too (tick them, or click them on the model). Fill Pattern copies features only. Feature folders. Right-click a feature ▸ Add to New Folder… (or Move to a folder already there, or Remove from Folder) to group features in the tree; a folder sits where its first feature is, with its features under it. Right-click a folder to rename it, delete it (its features stay), or make a Linear or Circular Pattern of the Folder. A pattern's More features list takes folders too: it copies whatever is in the folder each time it rebuilds, so a feature added to the folder later is copied as well. Library features. Right-click a feature or a feature folder ▸ Save as Library Feature… to keep it under a name in your settings, for any part: the feature with the sketches it uses (and, for a folder, everything in it), and the variables its sizes use. Features ▸ Library Feature puts it in the part you are in: choose it, set its variables (each copy gets variables of its own: a second copy's w becomes w_2), the angle to turn it about the face's normal, then click the plane or flat face for its first sketch. The copy goes into a folder of its name, and its features stay ordinary features you can edit. A feature that uses a plane, a body or projected geometry outside the group cannot be saved this way (put that in the group too). Patterns of cuts are cut out in one operation, and patterns of added features (bosses, pins, ribs) are fused into the body in one operation, so large patterns rebuild quickly. A plate with 200 bosses builds in about 2 seconds. A pattern or mirror of a sheet metal feature that makes a body (Base-Flange, SM-Extrude, Lofted-Bend, Transition) copies that body as it is at the pattern, with the flanges and cuts added to it so far. Each copy is sheet metal with its own flat pattern. A mirrored copy's flat pattern is the mirror image, with its bends going the other way. A mirrored lofted bend becomes a plain solid.

sections.title: Fillet
sections.text: Open the feature and click edges on the model. The model is rolled back to just before the feature so every edge can be picked; tick Preview to see the result. The radius accepts equations. Edges are remembered by type, direction and position, and found again after parameter changes. Where a fillet can't be added on top of earlier fillets (a corner where several blends meet), RazorCAD recomputes it together with the preceding fillets in one operation. Where two blends exactly meet (for example R2 on both edges of a 4 mm wall) the result is a full round. Variable size: a radius at the start and another at the end of each edge, or Radius ▸ At vertices and points along edges: the panel lists the vertices of the selected edges (the ends of each run of edges) with a radius for each; empty ones use the fillet's radius. Along each edge the radius changes from the one at its start to the one at its end. Points along the edges (with radii at the vertices): Add Point, then choose the edge, where along it (the share of its length from its start in %, or a distance from its start in mm) and the radius there; or Add by Clicking and click on the edge where the point goes. The radius runs smoothly from the edge's start through its points to its end. While the fillet is edited each point is marked on its edge, so you can see which end the % counts from; drag a mark along its edge to move the point (its % or mm follows, and the fillet rebuilds when you let go). Setback at corners: where three or more fillets meet, the corner is blended smoothly from this distance out, instead of the usual small corner patch. A little more than the radius works well; 0 keeps the usual corner. The fillet's note says how many corners were blended. Face fillet: pick faces instead of edges; the edges where they meet are rounded. Full round : click a side face, the face to round off, then the other side face (flat and parallel: a wall of even thickness). The middle face is replaced by one round meeting both sides, its radius half the wall's thickness. Size by → Chord width (constant size) : the value is the width across each fillet, from edge to edge; each edge's radius follows from how far its two faces turn (measured at its middle: exact between flat faces). Shape → Curvature continuous (G2) (constant size) : instead of a round (which meets the faces beside it in tangent but jumps from flat to curved), each blend leaves its faces with the same tangent plane and no curvature, then curves gradually: no visible line where it starts, as on styled housings and covers. It sets back from the edge as far as the round of that radius would, but stays closer to the sharp corner, so it takes less material away. The blend is exact (a curve of degree five swept along the edge, not a fitted patch). It is made on straight edges between flat faces whose ends meet flat faces, and on circular edges all the way round between a flat face and a round face on the same axis (the foot or top rim of a boss, a counterbore's edge: the section revolved round the axis); round corners and other curved edges in a fillet of their own. The note reports the tangent and curvature mismatch measured on the CAD faces. For a G2 patch over an opening use Filled Surface with Boundary continuity Curvature (G2); for G2 joins between lofted profiles use Loft → Across guide seams → G2. An edge's own size : each edge in the list has a box for a radius of its own (expressions allowed); blank uses the fillet's. One feature can so round edges with different radii in one go, corners and all. Add a face's edges: then click a face, and all its edges are added (clicked again, removed).
sections.html:
Open the feature and click edges on the model. The model is rolled back to just before the feature so every edge can be picked; tick Preview to see the result. The radius accepts equations.

  • Edges are remembered by type, direction and position, and found again after parameter changes.
  • Where a fillet can't be added on top of earlier fillets (a corner where several blends meet), RazorCAD recomputes it together with the preceding fillets in one operation.
  • Where two blends exactly meet (for example R2 on both edges of a 4 mm wall) the result is a full round.
  • Variable size: a radius at the start and another at the end of each edge, or Radius ▸ At vertices and points along edges: the panel lists the vertices of the selected edges (the ends of each run of edges) with a radius for each; empty ones use the fillet's radius. Along each edge the radius changes from the one at its start to the one at its end.
  • Points along the edges (with radii at the vertices): Add Point, then choose the edge, where along it (the share of its length from its start in %, or a distance from its start in mm) and the radius there; or Add by Clicking and click on the edge where the point goes. The radius runs smoothly from the edge's start through its points to its end. While the fillet is edited each point is marked on its edge, so you can see which end the % counts from; drag a mark along its edge to move the point (its % or mm follows, and the fillet rebuilds when you let go).
  • Setback at corners: where three or more fillets meet, the corner is blended smoothly from this distance out, instead of the usual small corner patch. A little more than the radius works well; 0 keeps the usual corner. The fillet's note says how many corners were blended.
  • Face fillet: pick faces instead of edges; the edges where they meet are rounded.
  • Full round : click a side face, the face to round off, then the other side face (flat and parallel: a wall of even thickness). The middle face is replaced by one round meeting both sides, its radius half the wall's thickness.
  • Size by → Chord width (constant size) : the value is the width across each fillet, from edge to edge; each edge's radius follows from how far its two faces turn (measured at its middle: exact between flat faces).
  • Shape → Curvature continuous (G2) (constant size) : instead of a round (which meets the faces beside it in tangent but jumps from flat to curved), each blend leaves its faces with the same tangent plane and no curvature, then curves gradually: no visible line where it starts, as on styled housings and covers. It sets back from the edge as far as the round of that radius would, but stays closer to the sharp corner, so it takes less material away. The blend is exact (a curve of degree five swept along the edge, not a fitted patch). It is made on straight edges between flat faces whose ends meet flat faces, and on circular edges all the way round between a flat face and a round face on the same axis (the foot or top rim of a boss, a counterbore's edge: the section revolved round the axis); round corners and other curved edges in a fillet of their own. The note reports the tangent and curvature mismatch measured on the CAD faces. For a G2 patch over an opening use Filled Surface with Boundary continuity Curvature (G2); for G2 joins between lofted profiles use Loft → Across guide seams → G2.
  • An edge's own size : each edge in the list has a box for a radius of its own (expressions allowed); blank uses the fillet's. One feature can so round edges with different radii in one go, corners and all.
  • Add a face's edges: then click a face, and all its edges are added (clicked again, removed).

sections.title: Chamfer
sections.text: Click edges as for a fillet. Chamfer types: equal distance, distance + angle or two distances. Flip direction swaps the sides. With equal distances each edge can have a distance of its own, and Add a face's edges works as for Fillet. Vertex (cut off a corner) : click corners of the model where three straight edges meet; each is cut off by the plane through the points the distance along each of its edges. Different distances along X, Y and Z gives the edges running most along X, Y and Z their own distances. A distance as long as its edge, or a corner in a recess (where the cut would add material), is refused.
sections.html:
Click edges as for a fillet. Chamfer types: equal distance, distance + angle or two distances. Flip direction swaps the sides. With equal distances each edge can have a distance of its own, and Add a face's edges works as for Fillet.

Vertex (cut off a corner) : click corners of the model where three straight edges meet; each is cut off by the plane through the points the distance along each of its edges. Different distances along X, Y and Z gives the edges running most along X, Y and Z their own distances. A distance as long as its edge, or a corner in a recess (where the cut would add material), is refused.

sections.title: Shell
sections.text: Click the faces to remove and set the wall thickness, inward or outward. With no faces removed, the body is hollowed: a closed void inside, the thickness in from the outside everywhere (a body too thin for it is refused). Hollowed outward, the body itself becomes the void and the walls are built round it, the thickness out from every face (edges and corners rounded). Walls of Their Own Thickness : Select walls in canvas, then click flat faces of the body: each wall gets a thickness of its own, more than the shell's (the box beside it). Inward, the material behind the face is kept down to that depth; outward, the face is built out to that thickness over its own outline. A removed face cannot have one (it is the opening). Shell validates the resulting solid and rejects a failed offset that merely returns the original full body. For inward shells, small fillets or chamfers can be retained outside with sharp corners inside; the feature note reports this construction. If no valid cavity can be made, reduce the thickness, select different removal faces, or place Shell before the fillets and chamfers.
sections.html:
Click the faces to remove and set the wall thickness, inward or outward. With no faces removed, the body is hollowed: a closed void inside, the thickness in from the outside everywhere (a body too thin for it is refused). Hollowed outward, the body itself becomes the void and the walls are built round it, the thickness out from every face (edges and corners rounded).

Walls of Their Own Thickness : Select walls in canvas, then click flat faces of the body: each wall gets a thickness of its own, more than the shell's (the box beside it). Inward, the material behind the face is kept down to that depth; outward, the face is built out to that thickness over its own outline. A removed face cannot have one (it is the opening). Shell validates the resulting solid and rejects a failed offset that merely returns the original full body. For inward shells, small fillets or chamfers can be retained outside with sharp corners inside; the feature note reports this construction. If no valid cavity can be made, reduce the thickness, select different removal faces, or place Shell before the fillets and chamfers.

sections.title: Draft
sections.text: Pick a neutral face, then the faces to tilt by an angle. Reverse tilts them the other way.
sections.html: Pick a neutral face, then the faces to tilt by an angle. Reverse tilts them the other way.

sections.title: Rib
sections.text: An open sketch line is thickened and filled out until it meets the model, either in the sketch plane (for example a gusset across a bracket corner) or square to it.
sections.html: An open sketch line is thickened and filled out until it meets the model, either in the sketch plane (for example a gusset across a bracket corner) or square to it.

sections.title: Dome
sections.text: A spherical cap or half ellipsoid on round faces, or a smooth dome filled over any other flat outline. Reverse presses it in.
sections.html: A spherical cap or half ellipsoid on round faces, or a smooth dome filled over any other flat outline. Reverse presses it in.

sections.title: Plastic part features
sections.text: Four features for moulded parts (Features tab). Mounting Boss : posts at clicked points on a flat face (or at a sketch's points and circle centres), rising out of the face: Outer diameter, Height, a Draft on the outside, a Hole (diameter, and a depth: empty for the full height), and Ribs: how many, their width, how far out from the boss and how high. Snap Hook : a cantilever beam (length, thickness, width) with a hook at its tip: its overhang, its lead-in angle from the beam (the slope it slides in on) and its catch angle (90°: square, holding; less: it lets go when pulled). Hook faces turns it about the face's normal. Lip / Groove : click the flat rim face along the open edge of a shelled part: a lip (raised) or groove (sunk), along its inner or outer edge, of a width and height (depth). For two halves that fit: a lip on one, on the other a groove a little wider and deeper. Vent : slots across a sketch's closed outline on a face, of a slot width with bars between them, at an angle, kept a margin in from the outline, cut through or to a depth.
sections.html:
Four features for moulded parts (Features tab).

  • Mounting Boss : posts at clicked points on a flat face (or at a sketch's points and circle centres), rising out of the face: Outer diameter, Height, a Draft on the outside, a Hole (diameter, and a depth: empty for the full height), and Ribs: how many, their width, how far out from the boss and how high.
  • Snap Hook : a cantilever beam (length, thickness, width) with a hook at its tip: its overhang, its lead-in angle from the beam (the slope it slides in on) and its catch angle (90°: square, holding; less: it lets go when pulled). Hook faces turns it about the face's normal.
  • Lip / Groove : click the flat rim face along the open edge of a shelled part: a lip (raised) or groove (sunk), along its inner or outer edge, of a width and height (depth). For two halves that fit: a lip on one, on the other a groove a little wider and deeper.
  • Vent : slots across a sketch's closed outline on a face, of a slot width with bars between them, at an angle, kept a margin in from the outline, cut through or to a depth.

sections.title: Core and Cavity
sections.text: Core and Cavity (Features tab) makes the two halves of a simple mould for the part : a block round it (Block margin beyond it every way), the part taken out of it grown by the Shrinkage (the plastic shrinks as it cools), split at a parting plane square to the Pull direction. The plane goes at the part's largest section along the pull (or At a height up the part). The half the pull direction points into is the Cavity, the other the Core; holes along the pull become shut-offs where the plane crosses them. Parting can also be a parting surface of your own (a surface body reaching past the block all round, made with the surface tools along the part's parting line): the block is split by it, the side the pull points into the cavity. Check the part with Draft Analysis and Undercut Check first. Side Core (after Core and Cavity) makes a side action for an undercut: click its faces on the part (a side hole, a catch) and the direction it is pulled (the first face's normal, or an axis). A block round the faces (grown by the margin), from the part out past the mould block, is taken out of the core and the cavity and made a body of its own, Side core. Sprue and Runners cuts round runners along the lines of a sketch on the parting plane (half in the core, half in the cavity; they gate into the part where they meet it) and a tapered sprue from the back of the cavity down to the start of the first line.
sections.html:
Core and Cavity (Features tab) makes the two halves of a simple mould for the part : a block round it (Block margin beyond it every way), the part taken out of it grown by the Shrinkage (the plastic shrinks as it cools), split at a parting plane square to the Pull direction. The plane goes at the part's largest section along the pull (or At a height up the part). The half the pull direction points into is the Cavity, the other the Core; holes along the pull become shut-offs where the plane crosses them. Parting can also be a parting surface of your own (a surface body reaching past the block all round, made with the surface tools along the part's parting line): the block is split by it, the side the pull points into the cavity. Check the part with Draft Analysis and Undercut Check first.

Side Core (after Core and Cavity) makes a side action for an undercut: click its faces on the part (a side hole, a catch) and the direction it is pulled (the first face's normal, or an axis). A block round the faces (grown by the margin), from the part out past the mould block, is taken out of the core and the cavity and made a body of its own, Side core.

Sprue and Runners cuts round runners along the lines of a sketch on the parting plane (half in the core, half in the cavity; they gate into the part where they meet it) and a tapered sprue from the back of the cavity down to the start of the first line.

sections.title: Move Face
sections.text: Push or pull flat faces along their normal, or turn a face about one of its edges. The neighbouring faces follow.
sections.html: Push or pull flat faces along their normal, or turn a face about one of its edges. The neighbouring faces follow.

sections.title: Delete or Resize Fillet, Defeature
sections.text: These edit a solid directly, with no history needed: good for imported parts. Delete / Resize Fillet (Surfaces tab): click fillet or chamfer faces. Delete carries the faces either side on until they meet at a sharp edge again; Resize then rounds (or chamfers) that edge at the New radius. The faces round them are grown or shrunk to close the gap exactly, so it works on most rounds and chamfers, including rounds that run into other rounds at a corner; the message says what the faces were (R2, chamfered, blended). When the faces cannot close the gap, it falls back to the simpler way: rounds along straight edges between flat faces (convex or concave), full rounds on circular edges (between a flat face and a round face, like the foot or top rim of a boss) and chamfers between flat faces, whose ends meet flat faces. Defeature takes every fillet up to a radius and every hole up to a diameter out of a body (or of every solid), for a simpler part to send to a supplier or to analyse. A hole is filled with its counterbore, countersink and drill point; one whose counterbore is wider than the limit stays whole. They are all taken out at once, exactly, the faces round them grown or shrunk to close the gaps (the message then says "taken out exactly"). If the kernel cannot close a gap, the body is done the simpler way, one at a time, and fillets whose ends do not meet flat faces, and holes that break out of the side of the part, stay; the message says how many were taken out.
sections.html:
These edit a solid directly, with no history needed: good for imported parts.

Delete / Resize Fillet (Surfaces tab): click fillet or chamfer faces. Delete carries the faces either side on until they meet at a sharp edge again; Resize then rounds (or chamfers) that edge at the New radius. The faces round them are grown or shrunk to close the gap exactly, so it works on most rounds and chamfers, including rounds that run into other rounds at a corner; the message says what the faces were (R2, chamfered, blended). When the faces cannot close the gap, it falls back to the simpler way: rounds along straight edges between flat faces (convex or concave), full rounds on circular edges (between a flat face and a round face, like the foot or top rim of a boss) and chamfers between flat faces, whose ends meet flat faces.

Defeature takes every fillet up to a radius and every hole up to a diameter out of a body (or of every solid), for a simpler part to send to a supplier or to analyse. A hole is filled with its counterbore, countersink and drill point; one whose counterbore is wider than the limit stays whole. They are all taken out at once, exactly, the faces round them grown or shrunk to close the gaps (the message then says "taken out exactly"). If the kernel cannot close a gap, the body is done the simpler way, one at a time, and fillets whose ends do not meet flat faces, and holes that break out of the side of the part, stay; the message says how many were taken out.

sections.title: Scale
sections.text: Scales every body by one factor, about the origin or about the centre of the bodies.
sections.html: Scales every body by one factor, about the origin or about the centre of the bodies.

sections.title: Long operations
sections.text: If a feature takes more than a few seconds, a banner above the model says what is being worked on ("Still working on Extrude Cut1 (12 s)…") with a Stop button (also next to the progress bar). Stop restarts the geometry kernel: a feature you are still editing is cancelled and a finished feature is suppressed, so you can unsuppress it to try again.
sections.html: If a feature takes more than a few seconds, a banner above the model says what is being worked on ("Still working on Extrude Cut1 (12 s)…") with a Stop button (also next to the progress bar). Stop restarts the geometry kernel: a feature you are still editing is cancelled and a finished feature is suppressed, so you can unsuppress it to try again.

sections.title: Solid bodies
sections.text: A part can contain several solid bodies. A boss that doesn't touch the existing material makes a new body; untick Merge result to keep a touching boss separate. A cut that slices a body in two leaves two bodies. The Solid Bodies (n) folder at the top of the tree lists the bodies: Click a body to select and highlight it. Double-click (or right-click ▸ Rename) to name it. Unnamed bodies are named after the last feature that changed them. Bodies are identified by the feature that created them, so names and materials stay attached when you change dimensions. Folders: right-click ▸ Add to New Folder or Move to folder to organise bodies. Identical bodies are listed once with their count (×N). Open the item to see each body. Right-click for Isolate, Hide or Show all of them. Identical means the same volume, surface area, principal moments of inertia, handedness and material (and for sheet metal, the same thickness and flat pattern).
sections.html:
A part can contain several solid bodies. A boss that doesn't touch the existing material makes a new body; untick Merge result to keep a touching boss separate. A cut that slices a body in two leaves two bodies.

The Solid Bodies (n) folder at the top of the tree lists the bodies:

  • Click a body to select and highlight it.
  • Double-click (or right-click ▸ Rename) to name it. Unnamed bodies are named after the last feature that changed them.
  • Bodies are identified by the feature that created them, so names and materials stay attached when you change dimensions.
  • Folders: right-click ▸ Add to New Folder or Move to folder to organise bodies.
  • Identical bodies are listed once with their count (×N). Open the item to see each body. Right-click for Isolate, Hide or Show all of them. Identical means the same volume, surface area, principal moments of inertia, handedness and material (and for sheet metal, the same thickness and flat pattern).

sections.title: Body Properties
sections.text: Right-click a body (tree or view) ▸ Body Properties…. It holds the body's name, material, description and any number of custom properties (name/value pairs such as part number or finish). It also shows the body's mass, volume, area and centre of mass. For sheet metal bodies it adds the sheet data (Sheet Metal chapter).
sections.html: Right-click a body (tree or view) ▸ Body Properties…. It holds the body's name, material, description and any number of custom properties (name/value pairs such as part number or finish). It also shows the body's mass, volume, area and centre of mass. For sheet metal bodies it adds the sheet data (Sheet Metal chapter).

sections.title: Materials
sections.text: The Material item in the tree sets the part material (Tools ▸ Edit Material…). A body set to Use part material follows it. A body given its own material keeps it when the part material changes and is drawn in that material's colour. Mass Properties adds up every body with its own density. The material list is in Appendix B.
sections.html: The Material item in the tree sets the part material (Tools ▸ Edit Material…). A body set to Use part material follows it. A body given its own material keeps it when the part material changes and is drawn in that material's colour. Mass Properties adds up every body with its own density. The material list is in Appendix B.

sections.title: Appearance
sections.text: Right-click a face ▸ Appearance… or a body ▸ Body Appearance… to give it a colour, or Default colour to set it back. Face colours stay with their face when the model changes. A body's own appearance wins over its material colour and over colours imported from a STEP file.
sections.html: Right-click a face ▸ Appearance… or a body ▸ Body Appearance… to give it a colour, or Default colour to set it back. Face colours stay with their face when the model changes. A body's own appearance wins over its material colour and over colours imported from a STEP file.

sections.title: Render and decals
sections.text: Evaluate ▸ Render makes a photorealistic picture of the view as it is now : choose the size (as the view, or up to 3840 × 2160), the Quality (Draft: one pass; Good: 16 passes, Best: 64, each with the view and the light moved a little and the passes averaged, for smooth edges and soft shadows), the lighting (Studio, Outdoor sky, or studio on white), a soft shadow on the floor and the exposure, and a look for each body: polished, brushed or cast metal, gloss paint, powder coat, glossy or matte plastic, rubber or glass, or From the material (aluminium and stainless brushed, steel cast, brass and copper polished, ABS glossy, PLA and nylon matte). Bodies keep their colours, and their looks are kept with them. Save PNG… writes the picture. Evaluate ▸ Decal puts a picture (a logo, a label) on a flat face: open the picture, give its width and angle, then click the face where its middle goes. Decals show in the view and in renders, are saved with the part, and are not geometry. Tools ▸ Decals… lists them, to delete them.
sections.html:
Evaluate ▸ Render makes a photorealistic picture of the view as it is now : choose the size (as the view, or up to 3840 × 2160), the Quality (Draft: one pass; Good: 16 passes, Best: 64, each with the view and the light moved a little and the passes averaged, for smooth edges and soft shadows), the lighting (Studio, Outdoor sky, or studio on white), a soft shadow on the floor and the exposure, and a look for each body: polished, brushed or cast metal, gloss paint, powder coat, glossy or matte plastic, rubber or glass, or From the material (aluminium and stainless brushed, steel cast, brass and copper polished, ABS glossy, PLA and nylon matte). Bodies keep their colours, and their looks are kept with them. Save PNG… writes the picture.

Evaluate ▸ Decal puts a picture (a logo, a label) on a flat face: open the picture, give its width and angle, then click the face where its middle goes. Decals show in the view and in renders, are saved with the part, and are not geometry. Tools ▸ Decals… lists them, to delete them.

sections.title: Exploded views of a part
sections.text: A part with two or more bodies can have exploded views: Insert ▸ Exploded View…, or right-click the Solid Bodies folder. Only the display moves; the model stays as it is. The steps are made as for an assembly (see Exploded views in the Assemblies chapter).
sections.html: A part with two or more bodies can have exploded views: Insert ▸ Exploded View…, or right-click the Solid Bodies folder. Only the display moves; the model stays as it is. The steps are made as for an assembly (see Exploded views in the Assemblies chapter).

sections.title: Combine and Subtract Bodies
sections.text: Combine joins bodies with Add, Subtract or Common; the first body clicked is the main body. Subtract Bodies picks a cutting body and target body; Consume cutting body (on by default) removes the cutting body afterwards.
sections.html: Combine joins bodies with Add, Subtract or Common; the first body clicked is the main body. Subtract Bodies picks a cutting body and target body; Consume cutting body (on by default) removes the cutting body afterwards.

sections.title: Split
sections.text: Cuts bodies into separate bodies with a plane, a flat face or a surface body. With a plane or face you can keep all the pieces or just the piece on one side.
sections.html: Cuts bodies into separate bodies with a plane, a flat face or a surface body. With a plane or face you can keep all the pieces or just the piece on one side.

sections.title: Move/Copy Bodies
sections.text: Moves or copies solid and surface bodies. By coordinates: ΔX/ΔY/ΔZ plus a rotation about X/Y/Z or a reference axis, through the axis or the bodies' centre. Copies repeat the step. With mates: Coincident, Distance, Parallel, Perpendicular, Angle and Concentric between an entity of the moving bodies (face, edge, vertex) and fixed geometry (another body, a plane, axis or point). Flip alignment turns a mate around.
sections.html:
Moves or copies solid and surface bodies.

  • By coordinates: ΔX/ΔY/ΔZ plus a rotation about X/Y/Z or a reference axis, through the axis or the bodies' centre. Copies repeat the step.
  • With mates: Coincident, Distance, Parallel, Perpendicular, Angle and Concentric between an entity of the moving bodies (face, edge, vertex) and fixed geometry (another body, a plane, axis or point). Flip alignment turns a mate around.

sections.title: Delete Body
sections.text: Removes a body from the model from that point in the history. Deleting the Delete Body feature brings the body back.
sections.html: Removes a body from the model from that point in the history. Deleting the Delete Body feature brings the body back.

sections.title: Surfaces
sections.text: The Surfaces tab builds surface bodies (zero-thickness faces), listed under Surface Bodies in the tree. Cuts and Combine only act on solid bodies; Knit, Thicken or Convert to Solid turn surfaces into solids.
sections.html: The Surfaces tab builds surface bodies (zero-thickness faces), listed under Surface Bodies in the tree. Cuts and Combine only act on solid bodies; Knit, Thicken or Convert to Solid turn surfaces into solids.

sections.title: Making surfaces
sections.text: Feature What it does --- --- Extruded Surface Extrudes selected regions, open/closed contours or individual entities; one side, symmetric total depth or independent depths on both sides; reverse supported Revolved Surface Revolves selected regions or open/closed contours with separate axis selection, optional axis projection and the same Full/Angle, one-side/two-side/symmetric controls as solid Revolve Planar Surface Creates flat surfaces from selected sketch regions, closed entity contours or coplanar model boundary edges; sketch regions preserve their holes Lofted Surface A surface through two or more profiles (sketches or 3D sketches), open or closed, optionally ruled (straight between profiles). Open profiles drawn in opposite directions are lined up automatically. Guide Curves (rails, optional): sketches or curves the surface follows between the profiles, e.g. along its edges; each runs from the first profile to the last, through every profile. One guide pulls the surface along it; two or more shape it across, each where it touches the profiles. Swept Surface An open or closed sketch profile, or a circle, swept along a sketch, 3D sketch, helix or chain of model edges. Orientation (including Square to faces), Twist angle, End scale and an optional Guide work as for Sweep (see Sweep and Sweep Cut); with a guide the profile can be open or closed. Closed profiles give a surface without end caps. Filled Surface A smooth patch over a hole bounded by one closed loop of edges of a surface or a solid, touching (G0), tangent (G1) or matching curvature (G2) with the faces round it; the condition can be set for each edge. It can be knit into the surface and close a solid. A flat loop gives a flat patch. Boundary Surface A surface through curves in two directions. The first and last curve of each direction bound it and must meet at their ends; the curves between shape it. Meeting other faces makes it tangent (G1) or curvature continuous (G2) to faces you pick (Select support faces): each bounding curve that runs along an edge of one of them meets that face so; the others just touch. It is checked on the CAD faces as for Filled Surface (contact 0.0001 mm, 0.5°, 0.001 1/mm) and the note gives what was measured. The curves must agree with the faces where they meet (a side curve leaving a G1 edge must leave along the face; for G2 its first three control points in line with it). Ruled Surface Straight-sided surfaces standing on edges, either normal to the surface or along a direction tapered by an angle, on one or both sides (for example mould parting surfaces) Offset Surface Offsets faces of any body Copy Surface Copies faces of any body as surface bodies, leaving the body unchanged. Join copies that touch into one surface body is on by default.
sections.html:
FeatureWhat it does
Extruded SurfaceExtrudes selected regions, open/closed contours or individual entities; one side, symmetric total depth or independent depths on both sides; reverse supported
Revolved SurfaceRevolves selected regions or open/closed contours with separate axis selection, optional axis projection and the same Full/Angle, one-side/two-side/symmetric controls as solid Revolve
Planar SurfaceCreates flat surfaces from selected sketch regions, closed entity contours or coplanar model boundary edges; sketch regions preserve their holes
Lofted SurfaceA surface through two or more profiles (sketches or 3D sketches), open or closed, optionally ruled (straight between profiles). Open profiles drawn in opposite directions are lined up automatically. Guide Curves (rails, optional): sketches or curves the surface follows between the profiles, e.g. along its edges; each runs from the first profile to the last, through every profile. One guide pulls the surface along it; two or more shape it across, each where it touches the profiles.
Swept SurfaceAn open or closed sketch profile, or a circle, swept along a sketch, 3D sketch, helix or chain of model edges. Orientation (including Square to faces), Twist angle, End scale and an optional Guide work as for Sweep (see Sweep and Sweep Cut); with a guide the profile can be open or closed. Closed profiles give a surface without end caps.
Filled SurfaceA smooth patch over a hole bounded by one closed loop of edges of a surface or a solid, touching (G0), tangent (G1) or matching curvature (G2) with the faces round it; the condition can be set for each edge. It can be knit into the surface and close a solid. A flat loop gives a flat patch.
Boundary SurfaceA surface through curves in two directions. The first and last curve of each direction bound it and must meet at their ends; the curves between shape it. Meeting other faces makes it tangent (G1) or curvature continuous (G2) to faces you pick (Select support faces): each bounding curve that runs along an edge of one of them meets that face so; the others just touch. It is checked on the CAD faces as for Filled Surface (contact 0.0001 mm, 0.5°, 0.001 1/mm) and the note gives what was measured. The curves must agree with the faces where they meet (a side curve leaving a G1 edge must leave along the face; for G2 its first three control points in line with it).
Ruled SurfaceStraight-sided surfaces standing on edges, either normal to the surface or along a direction tapered by an angle, on one or both sides (for example mould parting surfaces)
Offset SurfaceOffsets faces of any body
Copy SurfaceCopies faces of any body as surface bodies, leaving the body unchanged. Join copies that touch into one surface body is on by default.

sections.title: Guide control for Swept Surface
sections.text: Swept Surface uses the same separate canvas selectors and per-role Chain selection as solid Sweep. Choose one open or closed profile contour without holes; a region with inner loops must be reduced to the desired contour. Whole-sketch sources remain available explicitly for older workflows. Without a guide, Orientation and Twist angle work as in solid Sweep: perpendicular sections with an optional signed total twist, or sections parallel to the initial profile. Open and closed profiles remain uncapped. The same open, tangent-continuous path restriction and numerical checks apply to nonzero twist. Guide (optional) uses the same Orientation and Section size controls as the solid Sweep. Orientation keeps the profile dimensions; Section size uniformly scales the profile to follow the guide. Use one connected profile chain, open or closed, with an open path and guide. The guide must span the endpoint normal planes of the path; Section size also requires it to start on the profile curve and intersect every path normal plane once. Guide contact on the CAD surface is checked numerically to 0.0001 mm, using the same bounded scale-law refinement as solid Sweep. These are sampled numerical checks, not a certified global bound. Open profiles form a sheet. Closed profiles and the Circular option form an uncapped surface shell; no end caps or solid are added. Removing the guide restores the ordinary swept surface.

sections.title: Start and end conditions for Lofted Surface
sections.text: Lofted Surface uses the same Start Condition, End Condition, Influence and Reverse tangent direction controls described under Loft. Adjacent support faces can belong to solids or surfaces. Open profiles form a sheet; closed profiles form an uncapped shell. Guide curves can be combined with endpoint conditions using Adaptive approximation, with the same endpoint-tangent compatibility and sampled CAD contact checks as solid Loft.

sections.title: Guide construction for Lofted Surface
sections.text: Select Guide Curves → Guide construction → CAD constraints (two profiles) to use the original guide edges as patch boundaries. This supports open profiles forming a sheet, or closed profiles forming an uncapped surface shell. Guides can lie in different planes, making a nonplanar surface. A closed profile does not add end caps or make a solid. The kernel checks the patch contact error to 0.0001 mm, validates the resulting CAD shape and checks points on the guide curves independently. Across guide seams offers C0 (contact), G1 (tangency) and G2 (curvature continuity) along shared guide edges. G1 checks native CAD normals at nine interior positions, allowing at most 0.5° mismatch. G2 constructs a C2 B-spline surface for internal guide networks, trims the resulting patches and checks contact, normals and all three components of the second fundamental form at 33 independent positions on each seam. Its curvature mismatch limit is 0.001 1/mm. Measured angular and G2 curvature mismatches appear in the feature note. These are numerical tolerance checks, not a symbolic proof that every guide point is exact. The method requires two compatible profiles without holes or Thin Feature. Original profile corners are preserved. A transverse guide through a sharp corner cannot provide G2 continuity: choose C0 or move the contact onto a smooth profile segment. Circular profile seams are positioned automatically; straight guides already on a cylinder or cone preserve its geometry. Incompatible constraints report an error without lowering continuity or switching methods. Choose Adaptive approximation explicitly for other supported loft configurations.

sections.title: Surface Extrude and Revolve selection
sections.text: These commands use the same canvas profile/contour selector as Planar Surface and solid features. Turn off Chain selection for individual sketch entities and confirm the contour with Add selected contour. Unlike a solid profile, an open chain is valid. Selecting a region uses its boundary curves, including holes, without automatically using unrelated curves from its sketch. Closed contours remain surface shells; the command does not turn them into solids. Earlier whole-sketch features still rebuild and can be edited through the explicit whole-source fallback. Surface Revolve has separate profile and axis slots; the axis can come from another sketch. Surface Extrude's Symmetric depth is the total depth, while Two sides uses Depth and Second depth independently. Surface Revolve shares Full/Angle and one-side/two-side/symmetric behavior with solid Revolve, and goes Up To Vertex or Up To Surface too (a plane beside the axis trims it, as for solid Revolve). These surface commands create new surface bodies. Model edges and faces : besides sketch contours, both commands take edges of the model. Model Edges → Select model edges, then click edges on solids or surfaces (click again to remove one; Chain selection follows a surface body's open boundary). The edges join end to end into chains, open or closed; edges that branch are refused. Clicking a flat face of the model while choosing contours uses that face's outer and inner edges. Edges in one plane extrude square to it, out of the face they border when they lie on one; edges that do not lie in one plane, or a single straight edge, need Along (below). Surface Revolve revolves the chains about its axis, which must then be a reference axis, a model edge or face, or a line of a sketch. Surface Extrude start, end, direction and draft : Start from is the contour plane, an offset from it, or a plane / planar face, as for solid Extrude. Direction adds Up To Vertex, Up To Surface and Offset From Surface to One side, Two sides and Symmetric; an angled start or end surface trims the extrusion along it. Along chooses an axis to extrude along instead of square to the contours (None); Depth is then measured along it, and an axis that lies in the contours' plane is refused. Draft angle tilts the walls of closed contours about where the extrusion starts, each contour narrowing away from it (or widening with Draft outward), as for solid Extrude; an open contour of sketch lines and arcs leans to its left as drawn (Draft outward: to its right), each line and arc offset in the contour's plane as the extrusion rises, so its faces stay flat and conical.

sections.title: Planar Surface selection
sections.text: Use Sketch Profiles → Select profiles in canvas to click inside a closed region or select its contour. Each selection adds only that region, including its inner holes, instead of every profile in its sketch. Click a selected profile again to remove it. Chain selection follows connected sketch entities; turn it off to pick individual curves, then use Add selected contour once they close. Selecting just an outer contour fills that outline; click the actual region to include its holes. Use Model Boundary Edges → Select model edges for existing solid or surface edges. Choose one connected, closed, coplanar loop, with optional chain selection. The kernel rejects open, duplicate, missing or nonplanar boundary edges. Each selected sketch region creates a planar face; multiple independent regions are supported. Profiles remain linked to their source entities when dimensions change, and deleted selected entities require reselection. Existing whole-sketch features remain compatible. Other sources (whole sketch / curve) keeps whole-sketch selection available explicitly. A sketch with multiple regions no longer gets selected in full automatically when starting Planar Surface: choose the desired profiles in the canvas. Planar Surface creates flat sheets; use Filled Surface for a nonplanar patch or continuity to adjacent faces.
sections.html:
Use Sketch Profiles → Select profiles in canvas to click inside a closed region or select its contour. Each selection adds only that region, including its inner holes, instead of every profile in its sketch. Click a selected profile again to remove it. Chain selection follows connected sketch entities; turn it off to pick individual curves, then use Add selected contour once they close. Selecting just an outer contour fills that outline; click the actual region to include its holes.

Use Model Boundary Edges → Select model edges for existing solid or surface edges. Choose one connected, closed, coplanar loop, with optional chain selection. The kernel rejects open, duplicate, missing or nonplanar boundary edges. Each selected sketch region creates a planar face; multiple independent regions are supported. Profiles remain linked to their source entities when dimensions change, and deleted selected entities require reselection.

Existing whole-sketch features remain compatible. Other sources (whole sketch / curve) keeps whole-sketch selection available explicitly. A sketch with multiple regions no longer gets selected in full automatically when starting Planar Surface: choose the desired profiles in the canvas. Planar Surface creates flat sheets; use Filled Surface for a nonplanar patch or continuity to adjacent faces.

sections.title: Filled Surface / Patch continuity
sections.text: Select one connected, closed boundary loop. Chain selection is enabled for new patches: click an edge to add its connected boundary chain on that body; click a fully selected chain again to remove it. Turn the checkbox off to add or remove individual edges. Partial chains are completed without duplicate edges or changing existing per-edge continuity. Selection stops at branches; for solid edges, an explicitly selected support face can identify its boundary loop. The checkbox is saved with the feature; older files keep individual selection until enabled. Boundary continuity sets Contact (G0), Tangent (G1) or Curvature (G2) for the loop. Each edge can override that setting, so a patch can combine G0, G1 and G2 boundaries. Open, disconnected, duplicate or multiple loops report an error. Tangent reach : a tangent (G1) edge's row has a reach in mm (0 by default). With a reach, the patch also passes through points that far in from the edge along the support's tangent plane, so it keeps to that plane further before it turns towards the middle: a fuller, flatter rim. It applies to G1 edges only. Pass Through : Add a curve it passes through adds sketches, 3D sketches and curves lying inside the opening; Add points it passes through adds reference points, or a sketch's own points (those not on its curves). The patch passes through all of them as well as meeting its boundary; each is checked on the result to 0.0001 mm (the constraints are sampled more finely until it passes, or the patch reports how far off it is). G1/G2 edges require an adjacent support face. An open surface edge infers its unique adjacent face. Use Select support faces when a solid edge has two adjacent faces; exactly one selected adjacent face must cover each constrained edge. Select boundary edges returns to picking edges. G0 does not require support faces. Older files with Tangent enabled keep G1 behavior, with strict verification instead of a contact-only fallback. The resulting CAD face is checked for validity and sampled at 33 positions on each boundary: contact within 0.0001 mm, G1/G2 normal mismatch within 0.5°, and G2 mismatch of all three curvature components within 0.001 1/mm. Boundary trimming curves are checked again after knitting. Incompatible supports or failed constraints remain errors; the requested continuity is not downgraded. These checks are sampled numerical bounds, not a global mathematical proof. A latitude opening in a spherical face preserves its exact spherical continuation; other constrained patches use native plate construction with bounded refinement and final CAD checks. Knit into the surface joins the patch when all selected edges belong to one surface body. Make a solid when that closes it closes a watertight result; if other openings remain, the result stays a surface and its note says so. Example: tests/data/surface-patch-g2.rcad.

sections.title: Changing surfaces
sections.text: Feature What it does --- --- Trim Surface Cuts surfaces with a plane, a surface body or a sketch's curves (square to the sketch). Click the pieces to keep, or to remove. Mutual trims the tool surface too. Extend Surface Carries open edges straight on by a distance, following the surface's slope at the edge, and knits the extension on Untrim Surface Fills a surface's holes, or gives it back its natural extent (holes and outline). Pick faces to untrim only those. Knit Surface Sews surfaces together within a gap tolerance. When they enclose a volume, Try to form a solid turns them into a solid. Thicken Gives a surface a wall thickness (one side or both) and makes it a solid Delete Face Takes faces out of a solid or surface. Either leave the hole (the body becomes a surface body), patch each hole smoothly, optionally tangent, so the solid stays solid, or Heal: the faces round the hole grow or shrink until they meet and close it exactly, with no patch (a boss or a rib deleted as if it was never there). Good for removing fillets and bad faces from imported parts. Replace Face Moves flat faces of a solid onto a surface body, so the body grows or shrinks to meet it (for example a curved top). The surface must reach past the faces all round. Freeform Reshapes one face of a solid or surface by handles you push in or out (see below) Flatten Surface Unrolls faces of a surface or solid flat beside the model as a surface body (see below) Split (with a surface) Splits solid bodies with a surface body Move/Copy Surfaces As Move/Copy Bodies, for surfaces Delete Surface Removes a surface body

sections.title: Freeform
sections.text: Surfaces ▸ Freeform reshapes one face by a grid of handles. Click the face: a flat face of any outline, holes and all (the top of a block or a disc, a plate with holes), or a freeform face (a lofted or fitted face, or one Freeform has already reshaped). On a flat face with four straight edges or a freeform face that covers its whole surface, Keep at the edges sets what is held there. On any other face (another outline, holes, a trimmed freeform face) only the inside moves: the face stays as it was in a band along every edge and hole, so it always meets them in tangent plane and curvature (G2), and handles that fall outside its outline are left out (the note says how many are on the face). Rounds and other curved faces can't be reshaped yet. Set how many handles there are Across and Along the face (1 to 6 each): they sit evenly across it, and each Handle is how far the face is pushed out there (below 0, in), along its normal. The face passes through every handle exactly. Drag a handle on the model, in or out of the face, to move it; the face rebuilds when you let go. Keep at the edges says what the face keeps where it meets the faces round it: Contact (G0) (only the edges stay where they are), Tangent (G1) (the tangent plane along them too, so a face that ran smoothly into its neighbours still does; the default) or Curvature (G2) (the curvature as well). The more is kept, the closer to the middle the shape changes and the less it bulges. The face is made an exact B-spline surface and its control points are moved (the outer one, two or three rows of them held); the note gives how closely the handles are met and, measured on the CAD faces, how closely the tangent plane and curvature along the edges are kept. A face that would run through another face cannot be closed into the solid: use smaller heights.

sections.title: Curves and split lines
sections.text: Feature What it does --- --- Split Line Splits faces along a sketch's projection, or where a plane or surface crosses them. The body stays one body with its faces split, for example for a parting line, a draft or a colour. Projected Curve Projects a sketch along its normal onto faces, as a 3D curve Composite Curve Joins model edges end to end into one curve Projected and composite curves can be used as sweep paths, lofted surface profiles, curve-driven pattern paths and boundary surface curves.
sections.html:
FeatureWhat it does
